new_statements.rule_in_words: Hadhrami Arabic stress is quantity-sensitive and right-oriented like other Peninsular dialects: a final syllable containing a long vowel (superheavy, e.g. CVV.CVVC ṭaawúus 'peacock') takes the stress; otherwise stress falls on the penult (CV.CV́C.CVC ṣaːħíbkum 'your friend'; trisyllables without a final long vowel stress the penult); the authors add, after Bamakhramah 2010, that where two heavy syllables compete the leftmost one is stressed and that HA allows final-syllable extrametricality. This is an L2-acquisition paper's paraphrase, not a primary description.
new_statements.exceptions: None beyond the 'leftmost of two heavy syllables' clause and final-syllable extrametricality; no treatment of final CVCC, geminates, or light-only words (the 2023 thesis TOC shows a figure /ˈka.ta.ba/, /ˈkta.bu/ on p. 76 suggesting initial stress in all-light words, but that page was not accessible).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (lexical) stress of citation forms; examples are isolated nouns with suffixes (ṣaːħíb-kum).
new_statements.identity_note: hadr1236 covers the Arabic of Wadi Hadramawt and the Hadrami coast (Mukalla, Shihr). The quoted second-hand statement concerns 'Hadhrami Arabic (HA)' as spoken by Hadhramout-University undergraduates (sub-region unspecified) and rests on Bamakhramah 2010's HA data. Al-Saqqaf 1999 describes Wādī Ḥaḍramawt (inland) specifically; Habtoor 1989 describes Ġayl Ḥabbān (Shabwa governorate, west of Hadramawt proper), which Glottolog nonetheless lists under hadr1236. Landberg 1901 notes bedouin vs. sedentary (ḥaḍar) accent differences within Hadramawt (ribà' vs ríba, qurà' vs qùra).

sources.note: L2-English study of 69 Hadhrami-Arabic-speaking Yemeni undergraduates; pp. 538-539 and 555-556 summarise Hadhrami Arabic (HA) stress second-hand after Bamakhramah 2010: weight-driven, mostly right-headed; final syllable with a long ('tense') vowel always stressed (ṭaawúus CVV.CVVC); CV.CV́C.CVC ṣaːħíbkum penult; in trisyllables without a final long vowel the penult is stressed; HA 'permits extrametrical syllables'; with two heavy syllables stress goes to the leftmost.
